threads.body: There is an inconsistency in handling empty values between this code and `ParseContext.applyCommonParams`. In `ParseContext.applyCommonParams`, an empty `databasename` value falls through to `database` (due to the `databaseName.isEmpty()` check), but here only `containsKey` is checked—meaning an empty `databasename=` would be set and would NOT fall through to `database`. For consistency, consider also checking that the value is non-empty before accepting it, e.g., checking `urlParams.get(\"databasename\")` is not null/empty before setting it.

The `databasename`/`database` fallback resolution logic is duplicated between `JtdsUrlParser.parse` and `ParseContext.applyCommonParams`. Consider extracting this into a shared helper method (e.g., `resolveDatabaseNameParam(Map<String, String> params)`) to avoid the two implementations drifting apart if the resolution rules change in the future.

This test case is missing `.setSubtype(\"sqlserver\")`, which is present in the analogous jTDS test case at line 682. Both URLs have the same `jdbc:jtds:sqlserver://` prefix and should produce the same subtype. Without it, the expected subtype assertion for this case would be inconsistent.

threads.body: [General] `getDatabaseNameParam` is duplicated verbatim in `JtdsUrlParser` (lines 92-98). `UrlParsingUtils` already serves as the shared helper class for all parsers (e.g. `extractSemicolonParams`, `splitQuery`, `extractSubtype`). Moving `getDatabaseNameParam` there would eliminate the duplication and keep the two parsers in sync if additional aliases need to be added later.

[General] `applyDatabaseAliasParam` re-parses the semicolon-delimited URL parameters that were already parsed inside `applyCommonParams` on line 58 (both call `extractParams(jdbcUrl, ";", ";")`). Consider extracting the params map once in `parse()` and passing it to both `applyCommonParams` and the `database` fallback logic, or adding the `database` fallback directly into `applyCommonParams` (gated behind a parameter or MSSQL-specific flag) to avoid the redundant parse.

[General] The private `applyCommonParams` method here is a near-exact copy of `ParseContext.applyCommonParams` (lines 179-200). If that shared method is ever updated (e.g. to handle additional common properties), this copy will silently drift. Consider adding an overloaded `ParseContext.applyCommonParams(Map<String, String> params)` that accepts a pre-parsed map, so `MssqlUrlParser` can reuse it directly without duplication.
